label: copy-phase input e (fed-back e) in short sequences, not at the first copy step
explanation: Token-specific copy-phase feature: fires almost only when the input is the letter e being fed back during the copy phase (99.8% of activation mass is at in_tok=e in phase 2; never in the original phase or at the delimiter, never on first occurrences of a token). But only about 28% of copy-phase e inputs fire. Firing is strongly reduced when e is the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1) and in long sequences (L >= 7 has rate 0.4x and little mass). Peak is at recall_idx 3-4, i.e. e at original position 1-3 of a short (L=3..6) sequence. Top activations are e at orig position 1 in L=3-5 sequences (e.g. 2 e 2 <DEL> 2 [e]). Restricting to recall_idx>=2 and L<=6 gives dev F1 0.69 (P 0.71, R 0.67, mass recall 0.82). The residual precision gap is not explained by the next output token, absolute step, or to_go.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: e, u, c, w; input phase: ; delimiter step: ) and the token being output (most: c, 2, e, w, o, t; least: i, p, s, m); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=3, L=4 & t=6.
